candidates.statement: Gateway checkout returns 502 because the order service returns 502, which traces show originates from payment returning 503 on POST /v1/authorizations; the failure is a downstream server error propagated up the chain, not gateway-local.
candidates.uncertainty: Payment-side cause of the 503 (config, saturation, or dependency) is not observable from gateway evidence; only the propagation path is established.

report.explanation: All four checkout observations are 502s with short durations. Traces show a consistent chain: gateway /v1/checkout 502 <- order /v1/orders 502 <- payment /v1/authorizations 503, while inventory/reservations succeed. Logs confirm gateway client errors to order. This bounds the fault to a downstream server error surfaced as http-500, but the originating payment-side cause is not yet evidenced.
missing_evidence: Payment service logs/traces for POST /v1/authorizations explaining the 503 origin
Order service logs/traces showing why it maps payment 503 to 502
Payment and order resource metrics (CPU, connections, error rates) during the incident window
